source.title: Maximum Number of Occurrences of a Substring

teaching.hint: If a longer substring qualifies, what can you say about occurrences of its shortest permitted prefix?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Every occurrence of a valid longer substring supplies an occurrence of its valid length-`minSize` prefix, so some shortest permitted substring attains the optimum.
solution_outline.approach: Examine only windows of length `minSize`. Maintain their distinct-letter count and tally each valid window by its exact text; return the largest tally.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The moving window frequencies describe exactly the current length-`minSize` substring; each counted key records its number of starting positions seen so far.
solution_outline.correctness: A valid long substring cannot occur more often than its valid shortest prefix. Every shortest qualifying window is counted once, so the maximum tally equals the requested maximum.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(|s| * minSize)` time for materializing keys and `O(|s| * minSize)` worst-case storage for distinct keys; `minSize <= 26`.
solution_outline.pitfall: Checking every length up to `maxSize` can multiply work unnecessarily; overlapping occurrences still count.

common_wrong_turns: Assuming longer valid substrings may have a higher occurrence count
source_fidelity_notes: Removed repetitive examples; retained overlapping occurrences and both length and alphabet bounds.
